title: Tenant-aware signal decomposition and noise-robust alerting for usage/cost/latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a tenant-aware signal decomposition pipeline and a noise-robust alerting layer for usage, cost, and latency telemetry. The goal is to reduce false positive alerts for noisy tenants, provide per-tenant context in alert notifications, and enable progressive escalation policies that respect dedicated capacity and reserved commitments.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests raw usage/cost/latency timeseries and produces decomposed components (seasonal, trend, residual) per tenant within SLA
New anomaly scorer emits a single alert ticket with tenant context, root-cause candidates, and top correlated metrics for >80% of high-confidence anomalies
False positives reduced by >=40% on a held-out set of noisy tenants compared to current threshold-based rules
Alerting supports escalation tiers: info -> paging -> on-call, with rate-limits and suppression windows configurable per tenant or project
Dashboard and runbook link included automatically in alert payloads; integration tests for end-to-end flow pass in CI
work_items: Prototype decomposition using STL with downsampling and model selection for long-tail tenants
Implement tenant-level noise profile estimation and quantile-based adaptive thresholds
Add correlated-metric extraction job that runs at detection time (top-5 correlated signals)
Alert enrichment middleware: inject tenant billing plan, reserved capacity, recent deployments, and active rollouts
Extend existing alert router to support suppression rules and escalation policies by tenant label
Create Grafana dashboard and SLO monitor for pipeline latency and precision/recall on validation set
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after on-call spike where 3 noisy tenants generated 120 alerts in 30m; initial scoping with PM and SRE
2025-02-21: Proof-of-concept STL decomposition shows seasonal extraction for heavy tenants; added draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CO/tenant-signal-decomposition
2025-02-25: Benchmarked estimator on sample of 200 tenants; decomposition cost estimate ~0.8 vCPU per 24h per 1000 tenants when batched; discussed quantization and autoscaling with infra
2025-02-28: Implemented preliminary adaptive threshold prototype in staging; false positive reduction ~22% on small sample; pushed branch to GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2947
2025-03-03: Added correlated-metric extractor and alert enrichment stub; aligning on payload schema with notifications team; awaiting API contract review
decision_log: Use decomposition + residual scoring instead of only percentile thresholds to better handle nonstationary tenants
Prioritize tenant-level noise profiling over global thresholds for first launch to reduce ops noise
Alert payload will include a limited set of enrichment fields (tenant_plan, recent_deploy_commit, active_rollout_id) to balance payload size and utility
risks: Cost: decomposition and correlated-metric extraction can increase compute footprint; need batching and downsampling to control unit costs
Latency: on-demand decomposition at detection time may violate alert SLOs; plan to cache recent decompositions and run async fallbacks
Data quality: billing and deployment metadata may be missing for older tenants; fallback heuristics required
Ownership: cross-team dependencies for notification schema and runbook linking could delay rollout
next_steps: Complete API contract with notifications team (owner: Marco Lin) by 2025-03-06
Optimize batching and implement a 24h decomposition cache to meet 5s detection SLO
Run A/B evaluation on 1k tenants in prod-staging for 2 weeks and measure precision/recall
Prepare rollout plan with canary group and automatic rollback criteria
